# @smartput/query-introspect

A live database catalogue into a `@smartput/query` schema file you commit and
own. No runtime dependency at all — `Bun.SQL` speaks Postgres.

```sh
bunx @smartput/query-introspect --url postgres://… --out schema.ts
bunx @smartput/query-introspect --url postgres://… --out schema.ts --check
```

```ts
// Generated by @smartput/query-introspect from a postgres catalogue (shop, schema public).
// …
export const schema: Schema = defineSchema({
  tables: [
    {
      name: "orders",
      aliases: ["order", "purchase", "sale", "sales"],
      key: "id",
      columns: [
        { name: "status", as: "string", values: ["pending", "paid", "shipped"] },
        { name: "total_cents", kind: "money", unit: "usd", scale: 100 },
        // TODO: `_g` suggests { kind: "mass", unit: "g" }
        { name: "weight_g", as: "number" },
        { name: "placed_at", kind: "datetime" },
      ],
    },
  ],
  joins: [{ from: "orders.customer_id", to: "customers.id" }],
});
```

**Codegen, not runtime introspection**, and that is the whole design. A
catalogue proves table and column names, primary keys, foreign keys, enumerated
values, and the two kinds a type settles — `datetime` for a timestamp, `date`
for a date. It does not prove that `total_cents` is money, in what currency, or
by what factor. Nothing in `information_schema` distinguishes a number that is a
price from one that is a weight or a count.

A layer that guessed those at query time would answer a sentence with rows that
were silently wrong by a factor of a hundred, and — quoting
`packages/query/src/refusal.test.ts` — "a query that returns rows looks like it
worked". So every guess is emitted as a `TODO` comment above the column it is
about, where a person meets it before it can ever run. **No `kind` inferred from
a column name is ever written as a field.**

**Answers belong in the database.** A column comment beginning `@smartput` is
read and emitted directly, with no TODO, so the knowledge survives regeneration:

```sql
COMMENT ON COLUMN orders.total_cents IS
  '@smartput kind=money unit=usd scale=100 aliases=total, amount';
COMMENT ON TABLE orders IS '@smartput aliases=order, purchase, sale';
```

Columns take `kind`, `unit`, `scale`, `as`, `values`, `aliases` and `ignore`;
tables take `key`, `aliases`, `labels`, `geo` and `ignore`. A key this package
does not recognise is an error rather than a shrug — an annotation is a sentence
somebody wrote for this tool, so a typo in one is a typo, not a fact it cannot
map.

**`--check` is the half with the long-term value.** It reads the committed file
back and reports what the database has that the file does not: a new table, a
dropped column, a changed type, a foreign key with no join edge, a value the
enum gained. It exits non-zero, writes nothing ever, and is asymmetric on
purpose — a hand-written join across a soft foreign key, an extra alias, a
narrower `values` list are all the author's, and a check that nagged about them
is a check somebody turns off.

**Default mode refuses to overwrite** an existing file without `--force`,
because everything worth having in that file — a unit, an alias, a metric — is a
hand edit.

**A table with no primary key is left out**, with a note saying so. `TableDef.key`
is what `count` counts and what an aggregate groups by, and any column this
package picked would silently decide both. Add a key, annotate the table
`@smartput key=<column>`, or write the table in by hand.

**`@smartput/query` does not depend on this package and does not import it.** The
arrow runs one way: this writes a file, that reads the object the file makes.
Even `--check`, which has to read a committed `Schema` back, finds it
structurally rather than by importing the class.

**Two bin names, one file.** `query-introspect` is what `bunx
@smartput/query-introspect` resolves — a runner picks the bin matching the
unscoped package name — and `smartput-query-introspect` is the name worth having
on a global PATH.

Postgres only, done properly. A second dialect is one file that produces the
same `Catalog`; everything else is dialect-neutral by construction.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `--url <url>` | Connection URL. Defaults to `$DATABASE_URL`. |
| `--out <path>` | Where to write. Without it, stdout. |
| `--check` | Compare `<path>` against the database. Exits 1 on drift. |
| `--force` | Overwrite an existing `<path>`. |
| `--schema <name>` | Database schema to read. Default `public`. |
| `--name <ident>` | Name of the exported binding. Default `schema`. |
| `--exclude <table>` | Leave a table out. Repeatable, honoured by `--check`. |

Full documentation: [Querying a database](https://smartputs.dev/packages/query).
